modules.title: Introduction to Trade Networks and Slavery
modules.html:
Trans-Saharan and Atlantic trade, the slave trade and its effects on Nigeria. This section covers introduction to trade networks and slavery.

Key points

  • Which of the following was the primary commodity of the Trans-Saharan trade in the Sudanic region — Salt.
  • The 'Manila' was a form of _____ used in pre-colonial West African trade. — currency.
  • The most significant consequence of the abolition of the Trans-Atlantic Slave Trade was the _____. — rise of 'legitimate' trade in palm oil.
  • The Trans-Saharan trade route connected West Africa primarily with _____. — North Africa and the Mediterranean.
  • The 'Aro' people dominated the slave trade in Eastern Nigeria by using the _____. — Ekpe Society and the Long Juju.

Worked examples

Q: Which of the following was the primary commodity of the Trans-Saharan trade in the Sudanic region?
A: Salt — Salt was a crucial commodity brought from the Sahara (like Bilma and Taodeni) to the Sudan in exchange for gold.

Q: The 'Manila' was a form of _____ used in pre-colonial West African trade.
A: currency — Manillas were C-shaped metal bracelets (usually copper or brass) that served as a dominant currency in the Bight of Benin and Biafra.

quiz.q: Which of the following was the primary commodity of the Trans-Saharan trade in the Sudanic region?
quiz.solution: Salt was a crucial commodity brought from the Sahara (like Bilma and Taodeni) to the Sudan in exchange for gold.

quiz.q: The 'Manila' was a form of _____ used in pre-colonial West African trade.
quiz.solution: Manillas were C-shaped metal bracelets (usually copper or brass) that served as a dominant currency in the Bight of Benin and Biafra.

quiz.q: The most significant consequence of the abolition of the Trans-Atlantic Slave Trade was the _____.
options: rise of 'legitimate' trade in palm oil
quiz.solution: As the slave trade ended, West African economies shifted to exporting raw materials like palm oil, cocoa, and groundnuts to meet European industrial needs.

quiz.q: The Trans-Saharan trade route connected West Africa primarily with _____.
quiz.solution: The routes across the desert linked West African kingdoms with North African cities like Fez, Tunis, and Cairo.

quiz.q: The 'Aro' people dominated the slave trade in Eastern Nigeria by using the _____.
options: Ekpe Society and the Long Juju
quiz.solution: The Aro network leveraged their oracle and secret societies to control trade routes and supply slaves to the coast.

quiz.q: The primary commodity of the Trans-Saharan trade from the Sudanic region to North Africa was _____.
quiz.solution: Gold was the most sought-after commodity from West Africa, traded for Saharan salt and Mediterranean goods.

quiz.q: The ancient city-state of Kano became a major commercial hub primarily due to the _____ trade.
quiz.solution: Kano was the southern terminal for many Saharan trade routes, famous for its leather and textile industries.

quiz.q: Which of the following was a major consequence of the abolition of the Slave Trade?
options: End of all wars in Africa
Rise of 'Legitimate Commerce' like palm oil
quiz.solution: The end of human trafficking led to the export of raw materials required by European industries.

quiz.q: The 'Aro' people dominated the trade in Eastern Nigeria through the influence of the _____ oracle.
quiz.solution: The Long Juju oracle at Arochukwu gave the Aro the judicial and spiritual authority to control trade routes.

quiz.q: The trans-Atlantic slave trade is also known as the _____ trade.
quiz.solution: It involved a three-legged journey between Europe (manufactured goods), Africa (slaves), and the Americas (raw materials).
